title: French Onion Soup for the Hall
displayTitle: French Onion Soup for the Hall
seoTitle: French Onion Soup for the Hall | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Dark onion broth with a broiled Gruyère cap
subtitle: Dark onion broth with a broiled Gruyère cap
description: Dark onion broth with a broiled Gruyère cap. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

ingredients.name: Yellow Onions
ingredients.notes: halved pole to pole, sliced ¼ inch

steps.title: Caramelize onions low and slow
steps.instruction: Melt butter in a large Dutch oven over medium-low. Add onions with salt and cook, stirring every few minutes, until deeply golden brown and jammy, 45–60 minutes — do not rush over high heat or they burn before sweetening. The pot should smell sweet, not acrid.

steps.title: Deglaze and add stock
steps.instruction: Stir in sherry, scraping browned bits. Simmer until almost dry, 2–3 minutes. Add beef broth, chicken broth, thyme, bay leaves, and pepper. Bring to a simmer and cook 20 minutes. Broth should taste rich and onion-sweet; consistency is thin soup, not gravy.

steps.title: Toast baguette rounds
steps.instruction: Arrange baguette slices on sheet pans. Toast at 400°F until dry and lightly golden, 8–10 minutes — dry bread floats and soaks broth without turning mushy. Hold at room temp up to 4 hours.

steps.title: Fill crocks and top with cheese
steps.instruction: Heat broiler with rack 6 inches from element. Ladle hot soup into oven-safe bowls or crocks, leaving ½ inch headspace. Float 2–3 baguette crouton rounds per bowl and blanket with Gruyère — cheese should cover croutons to the rim so it melts into a solid cap.

steps.title: Broil the cheese cap and serve
steps.instruction: Broil until cheese bubbles and browns in spots, 3–5 minutes — watch constantly, no distracted tones during this step. Serve immediately with extra pepper at the line. Hold finished crocks in a warm box up to 20 minutes; re-broil 1 minute if cheese sets.

proTips: Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
tonightSpread: Keep the pot on low simmer on the stove — ladle from the side so the bottom doesn't scorch.
Set shredded cheese, crackers, and hot sauce in a row beside the pot.
Line up French Onion Soup for the Hall on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Dark onion broth with a broiled Gruyère cap. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Ground turkey swaps 1:1 for beef in chili if the crew wants leaner.
